source: ESPN NBA league injury designations plus NBA game lineup state

freshnessPolicy.missingReportMeaning: No injury report was matched; this is not a confirmed healthy designation.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Allen (concussion-like symptoms) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Lakers.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: With Allen on the shelf, Royce O'Neale and Christian Anderson should see a boost in minutes off the Hornets' bench. Allen's next chance to suit up will come Friday versus the Hawks.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Knueppel (hamstring) was diagnosed with a left hamstring strain Sunday and will be re-evaluated in four weeks.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Knueppel missed the first eight games of the 2026-27 campaign. He returned for the 114-104 loss to Brooklyn on Wednesday, though he exited the contest after just six minutes of work and didn't return. With Knueppel out of commission for at least a month, Grayson Allen and Sion James are candidates to replace him in the starting lineup, especially with Dennis Schroder (hamstring) sidelined for a minimum of two weeks.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Schroder has been diagnosed with a left hamstring strain and will be reevaluated in two weeks, Michael Scotto of HoopsHype.com reports.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Schroder, who missed Friday's game due to what was described as a left thigh injury, has been diagnosed with a hamstring strain. He is set to be reevaluated in two weeks, suggesting he will miss at least the next five games. Christian Anderson and Sion James could see extra minutes with Schroder sidelined.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Niederhauser (foot) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Jazz.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Niederhauser has yet to make his season debut for the Clippers while recovering from Lisfranc surgery on his right foot. He should still be considered week-to-week until stated otherwise.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Ingram (Achilles) won't play in Friday's game against the Thunder, per Law Murray of The Athletic.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Ingram is ramping up his activity as he nears his season debut for the Clippers, but he's not yet cleared for game action amid his Achilles rehab. Until the star forward is ready to suit up, Kris Dunn, Rui Hachimura and Derrick Jones should all hang onto starting roles.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Beal (knee) will not be ready for the start of the regular season, NBA writer Justin Russo reports.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Beal is dealing with knee inflammation that will keep him sidelined for Opening Night. While it's unclear how long the Clippers will be without the veteran guard, Darius Garland, Keaton Wagler and Kris Dunn should dominate the backcourt minutes in his absence. Beal's 2025-26 campaign was cut short by a hip injury after he averaged 8.2 points and 1.7 assists in 20.6 minutes across just six regular-season appearances.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Miller underwent surgery Wednesday to repair a torn left rotator cuff and will be re-evaluated in six months, per Law Murray of The Athletic.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: It's a tough break for Miller, who had an opportunity to battle for a reserve role during training camp in the fall. The timeline for a return is likely to keep him on the shelf until after the All-Star break. Miller's extended stay on the sidelines gives Kobe Sanders a chance to crack the Clippers' rotation.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Pullin (quadriceps) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against Portland.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Pullin will miss Tuesday's contest with a right quadriceps contusion, though his absence shouldn't affect the rotation. His next chance to play will come Thursday against New York.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Kuminga (shoulder) is out for Tuesday's game against Portland.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Kuminga sustained a bruised shoulder during Monday's meeting with the Trail Blazers, and he's sitting out the second part of this back-to-back set. Terrence Shannon appears to be the most likely candidate to replace Kuminga in the starting lineup, while Trey Lyles and Bones Hyland will both have a chance to claim a larger role.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Clark (hamstring) has been ruled out for the next two weeks.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Clark suffered a right hamstring strain during Saturday's 117-106 loss to Chicago. He played three minutes as a result of the injury, and he's now slated to miss at least two weeks and will be re-evaluated at that time. Terrence Shannon Jr. and Bones Hyland will see increased playing time off the bench in Clark's absence.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Edwards underwent a successful arthroscopic procedure on his right knee Thursday, the Timberwolves announced.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Edwards underwent debridement surgery in Minnesota, though the team did not provide a timetable for his return. The star guard is expected to make a full recovery, with additional updates coming as he progresses through rehabilitation. Based on previous reporting from ESPN's Shams Charania, Edwards could miss up to two months. Edwards was off to a scorching start this season, averaging 33.3 points, 4.8 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 2.0 steals across four appearances.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: DiVincenzo (Achilles) remains confident that he'll return during the 2026-27 season, Jon Krawczynski of The Athletic reports.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: DiVincenzo is approaching six months since tearing his right Achilles during the first round of the playoffs and has been rehabbing with the expectation that he'll play at some point this season. The veteran guard has sought advice from Jayson Tatum, Tyrese Haliburton and Damian Lillard during his recovery, though Minnesota has yet to establish a timetable for his return.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Avdija (foot) won't play Tuesday versus Minnesota.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Avdija scored 27 points over 30 minutes in Monday's loss to the Timberwolves. However, he won't be on the floor for Tuesday's rematch. As a result, Scoot Henderson and Jrue Holiday are candidates for more work, with one of those players expected to enter the starting lineup.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Youngblood (heel) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game at Minnesota.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Youngblood will miss a fourth consecutive contest with what the team is now calling a right heel bone bruise. His next opportunity to play will come Thursday at Milwaukee.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Krejci underwent surgery on his fractured left ankle Wednesday and will be re-evaluated in eight weeks, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Krejci suffered the ankle injury in last Wednesday's win over the Suns and is set to miss an extended period after undergoing surgery. With the 26-year-old and Ja Morant (hamstring) both on the shelf, Jrue Holiday and Sidy Cissoko should continue seeing increased minutes.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Head coach Micah Nori said Morant met with a doctor in Los Angeles, who gave him a positive outlook on his recovery from the hamstring injury. While Nori declined to update Morant's timetable, he added Morant "may not be out for as long as we thought," Trail Blazers Insider Sean Highkin reports.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Morant was initially given a four-week timetable after he suffered a Grade 2 left hamstring strain on Oct. 30. It sounds like he's making solid progress, though it would be surprising to see him beat that timetable given the tricky nature of hamstring injuries. Scoot Henderson will continue to start in his absence and there will be more minutes available for Jrue Holiday.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Sharpe suffered a torn meniscus in his knee and is expected to miss six months, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: It's a tough blow to the Trail Blazers' depth on the wing ahead of training camp. Sharpe, who is now likely to be sidelined until after the All-Star break, had been ticketed for a reserve role behind Toumani Camara following an injury-plagued 2025-26 campaign, which saw average a career-high 20.8 points, 1.4 steals and 2.1 three-pointers per game over 50 regular-season appearances. The door is now open for Vit Krejci and Jeremy Sochan to compete for bench minutes during camp.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Harper left Tuesday's game against the Spurs due to an undisclosed injury after an awkward fall, Chris Mannix reports.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: The injury occurred with only 53.6 seconds remaining in the fourth quarter, and Harper stayed down in pain for several minutes before being helped back to the locker room. He tallied 20 points (8-14 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 4-5 FT), four rebounds and two assists in 35 minutes prior to his exit, and we'll have to wait for an update on his status moving forward.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Harris (calf) is likely to be sidelined until early December, per Jeff Garcia of KENS 5 San Antonio.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Chris Haynes of NBA TV reported Friday that Harris is expected to ramp up his activity this week, and that the veteran forward could make his season debut as soon as early December. Until Harris is finally cleared to return from a calf strain, Julian Champagnie should continue to handle an expanded role on the wing.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Quaintance has been around the team but has not yet been cleared for basketball activities, Matt Guzman of SI.com reports.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: The Spurs are expected to exercise extreme caution with the big man, as Quaintance suffered a torn ACL and meniscus with Arizona State in February 2025 before appearing in only four games with Kentucky last season due to severe complications and persistent swelling. The 19-year-old underwent a cleanup procedure on his meniscus in mid-July, and the Spurs will likely want him at 100 percent before ramping him up to basketball activities.

injury.shortComment: Merrill (elbow) is questionable to face the Grizzlies on Wednesday.
injury.detail: Merrill has missed the past six games due to a right elbow issue, but this is the first time he's received the questionable tag since going down, which indicates progress. If he is cleared to return, Meleek Thomas' minutes could dip.

injury.shortComment: Mobley will receive treatment and participate in rehab after the team confirmed a diagnosis of a right great toe sprain, and he'll be re-evaluated in the next 7-to-10 days.
injury.detail: Mobley is set to miss his third straight game Monday since suffering the injury, and he's slated to miss at least the next week while on the mend. The Cavs should have a better idea on when he'll return to the court as he begins to progress through the treatment and rehab phase.

injury.shortComment: Tomlin (back) will remain on the inactive list for Wednesday's game against the Grizzlies.
injury.detail: Tomlin, who is recovering from a lower back stress reaction, has yet to suit up for the Cavs this season. He continues to get ruled out 24 hours in advance of tipoff, indicating he's still not close, so he can be viewed as week-to-week moving forward.

injury.shortComment: Tyson (ankle) is listed as doubtful for Wednesday's game against the Grizzlies.
injury.detail: Tyson is expected to miss a second consecutive contest with a right ankle injury. If Peyton Watson (back), who is listed as questionable, and Tyson are both ruled out, Meleek Thomas, Tyrese Proctor and Mario Hezonja could all see increased burn.

injury.shortComment: Watson (back) is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against Memphis.
injury.detail: Watson is listed on the injury report with a low back contusion after taking a hard fall in Monday's win over the Bulls. With Jaylon Tyson (ankle) doubtful to play Wednesday, Tyrese Proctor, Mario Hezonja and Meleek Thomas could all see increased playing time if Watson is ruled out.

injury.shortComment: Jackson underwent a procedure Wednesday to repair a broken fifth metatarsal in his left foot. He is expected to recover fully and will be re-evaluated in approximately three months.
injury.detail: Jackson suffered a foot injury in Saturday's 129-110 win over the Nets. Head coach Tuomas Iisalo indicated after the game that the injury was "relatively serious," though it is now confirmed he will miss extended time. While Jackson is out of commission, Taylor Hendricks and Jerami Grant should receive more playing time.

injury.shortComment: Jerome (hip) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game in Cleveland.
injury.detail: This will be Jerome's third straight game on the inactive list due to the hip injury, and for now, he should be considered questionable for Thursday's meeting with the Warriors. Cam Spencer should continue to start in his absence and Javon Small will have the chance for some extended minutes. Cedric Coward should continue to see some increased playmaking responsibilities with Jerome sidelined.

injury.shortComment: Pippen (back) is progressing in his recovery but is still considered week-to-week.
injury.detail: Pippen hasn't played since Oct. 29 due to a lumbar disc herniation and remains without a firm timetable to return.  Cam Spencer and Javon Small will likely continue seeing increased playing time in Pippen's absence.

injury.shortComment: Saunders signed a two-way contract with the Grizzlies on Saturday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
injury.detail: Saunders is still on the mend from a torn right ACL that he suffered during his final year at BYU. However, he has been cleared for on-court activities and will be allowed to practice with the Grizzlies now that he's officially signed with the team.

injury.shortComment: Stewart (illness) won't play Wednesday against the Cavs.
injury.detail: This will be Stewart's second straight game on the sidelines, which should lead to more minutes for Taylor Hendricks and Quinten Post. Stewart's next chance to play will come Thursday against the Warriors.

injury.shortComment: Furphy (knee) is practicing with the G League's Noblesville Boom, per Alex Golden of SI.com.
injury.detail: The Pacers have been pretty quiet regarding Furphy's ACL recovery since the offseason, but it's encouraging to hear some form of progress as the forward begins to ramp up his activity. Although Furphy still lacks a firm timetable for a return and is likely to be brought back slowly, it appears a season debut before the start of the new calendar year is in the cards.

injury.shortComment: Head coach Rick Carlisle said Tuesday that Haliburton (hamstring) is "getting there," but there's still no definitive timetable for his return to game action, Dustin Dopirak of The Indianapolis Star reports.
injury.detail: Carlisle wouldn't rule out a return in November, though he added that there's "nothing happening in the near-term." The star point guard hasn't played since Oct. 26 due to a left hamstring strain, and until he's cleared to return, Andrew Nembhard should continue seeing increased on-ball duties while Quenton Jackson sees increased burn.

injury.shortComment: McConnell (hamstring) is probable to play Wednesday against the Rockets.
injury.detail: McConnell's minutes have been steadily ramping up since he made his regular-season debut on Nov. 7, and he had his best game yet in Sunday's 131-124 loss to the 76ers, finishing with 12 points, five rebounds, five assists and one steal in 19 minutes off the bench. As long as Tyrese Haliburton (hamstring) is sidelined, McConnell should be able to earn enough minutes to provide some low-end value in fantasy leagues with his output in assists and steals.

injury.shortComment: Nembhard (hip) is questionable for Wednesday's game against Houston.
injury.detail: Nembhard is looking to end a one-game absence Wednesday with a hip injury. Another absence for Nembhard would likely result in a second consecutive start at point guard for Quenton Jackson, who tallied a season-high eight assists his last time out versus the 76ers.

injury.shortComment: Head coach Rick Carlise confirmed Sheppard will miss "months" after undergoing surgery to repair a torn meniscus in his left knee, Tony East of Forbes.com reports.
injury.detail: Sheppard required a full repair and is without a definitive timetable for a return to action. With Tyrese Haliburton (hamstring) expected to miss at least two weeks, Quenton Jackson figures to see a significant uptick in playing time. Two-way player Braden Smith could also see increased action with the parent club.

injury.shortComment: Capela (ankle) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against Indiana.
injury.detail: Capela is still recovering from a right ankle sprain and will remain on the inactive list for a ninth straight game. The veteran center's next opportunity to play will come Friday at Denver.

injury.shortComment: Thompson (knee) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Pacers.
injury.detail: Thompson is looking to end a one-game absence Wednesday due to a knee issue. Reed Sheppard has a chance to play a considerable role off the bench if Thompson sits out.

injury.shortComment: Adebayo (hip) is probable for Wednesday's game against the Bucks, per Ira Winderman of the South Florida Sun Sentinel.
injury.detail: The star big man was pulled as a precaution Monday against Houston due to a hip issue, and he's not expected to miss more time. After scoring in double figures in nine consecutive appearances prior to Monday's abbreviated outing, Adebayo will be aiming to start a new double-digit points streak Wednesday.

injury.shortComment: Gardner (hamstring) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Bucks, per Ira Winderman of the South Florida Sun Sentinel.
injury.detail: Gardner is battling a hamstring injury ahead of Wednesday's action. With Pelle Larsson (illness) available, Gardner's short-term fantasy appeal appears to be expiring.

injury.shortComment: Jovic (illness) is listed as probable for Wednesday's game against Milwaukee, Ira Winderman of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
injury.detail: Jovic is trending in the right direction following a one-game absence due to an illness. However, his return wouldn't cause any significant waves in the rotation.

injury.shortComment: Dieng will undergo a procedure to repair a fractured left finger Monday, Justin Garcia of the Milwaukee Bucks Radio Network reports.
injury.detail: Dieng was recently diagnosed with a fractured left finger, and the team has determined that he'll need to go under the knife to repair the injury. Milwaukee has yet to provide a timeline for his return, though more information should become available following the procedure.

injury.shortComment: Banchero is expected to be sidelined for the next four-to-six weeks due to a right high-ankle sprain, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
injury.detail: Banchero left during Friday's loss against the Timberwolves due to an ankle injury, and follow-up tests have confirmed a high-ankle sprain for the fifth-year forward. With an extended absence expected, the Magic will have to rely more heavily on Franz Wagner and Desmond Bane offensively, and Tristan da Silva figures to be the top candidate to enter the Magic's starting lineup for as long as Banchero is sidelined.

injury.shortComment: Isaac (knee) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Celtics.
injury.detail: Isaac's 2026-27 season debut will have to wait, as he's still working his way back from a left knee injury. He should be considered week-to-week until Orlando provides a clear update for his return.

injury.shortComment: Head coach Sean Sweeney said Wednesday that Nelson (ankle) has been doing "some on-court stuff," though Sweeney added that the work has been "minimal," Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
injury.detail: Nelson underwent surgery this offseason to repair a fractured left ankle. It's encouraging to hear that he's made some progress, but the two-way player can still be considered week-to-week moving forward.

injury.shortComment: Penda (hamstring) is making progress but remains without a timetable to return to game action, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
injury.detail: Penda suffered a partially torn hamstring in the preseason and can still be considered week-to-week moving forward. With the second-year forward and Paolo Banchero (ankle) both sidelined, Tristan da Silva and Jamal Cain should continue seeing increased minutes.

injury.shortComment: Barlow (back) is out for Wednesday's game against Orlando.
injury.detail: Barlow will be re-evaluated later this week and is thought to be closing in on his season debut, but he's not ready for game action quite yet. His next chance to return from a stress reaction in his back comes Saturday versus the Bucks.

injury.shortComment: Bona (back) will be re-evaluated in approximately one week after seeing a specialist, Ky Carlin of USA Today reports.
injury.detail: The fact that Bona needed to see a specialist suggests the injury may be more significant than initially thought, and he'll remain sidelined for at least the next several games. Even when healthy, the big man has seen his role shrink with Joel Embiid (foot) back in the rotation, averaging just 0.7 points, 1.7 rebounds and 1.0 blocks in four appearances outside of his 25-minute effort against the Pistons in late October. In Bona's absence, Jabari Walker could see a few more minutes as Philadelphia's backup center.

injury.shortComment: Brown is out for Wednesday's game against the Magic with a left hamstring strain.
injury.detail: The severity of the issue is unknown, but it seems like the 76ers are viewing the star forward as day-to-day for the time being. More usage should fall onto the plates of Tyrese Maxey, Joel Embiid and LeBron James for as long as Brown is sidelined.

injury.shortComment: Hukporti has sustained a season-ending ruptured right Achilles tendon, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
injury.detail: Hukporti went down with an Achilles injury in Monday's preseason opener against the Knicks, and an MRI has since revealed a rupture. He signed a one-year deal with the 76ers over the summer, so Hukporti will be an unrestricted free agent come season's end. With Hukporti's year already finished, Adem Bona (foot) should assume the backup center role behind Joel Embiid once healthy.

injury.shortComment: Awaka (back) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Nets.
injury.detail: Awaka is missing a fifth straight contest due to a back problem. The rookie big man can be considered week-to-week going forward.

injury.shortComment: Williams (finger) is listed as probable for Wednesday's game against Brooklyn.
injury.detail: After suffering a dislocated right pinky finger in Monday's loss to the Cavaliers, Williams is expected to play Wednesday. The 25-year-old forward is averaging 7.8 points, 3.2 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 0.8 steals across 22.7 minutes per contest in six regular-season appearances.

injury.shortComment: Wilson (hand) is expected to miss four to six weeks, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
injury.detail: The rookie forward went down during Wednesday's loss to the Spurs, and he now needs surgery to repair a fractured right hand. More pressure will likely fall on Josh Giddey going forward, while the likes of Tre Jones and Isaac Okoro will have a chance for added streaming value.

injury.shortComment: Bittle (foot) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Knicks, Zulfi Sheikh of Sportsnet.ca reports.
injury.detail: Bittle is still working his way back from a foot fracture that has plagued him for multiple months, and he remains without a clear return timeline. He can be considered week-to-week for the time being.

injury.shortComment: Leonard (knee) has progressed in his strength and conditioning program but will miss at least one more week, Michael Scotto of HoopsHype.com reports.
injury.detail: Leonard last played Oct. 23 due to left knee swelling but is seemingly nearing a return to action. The star forward will likely operate under a minutes restriction upon his return, but until then, Ja'Kobe Walter, Allen Graves and Collin Murray-Boyles should continue to see increased playing time.

injury.shortComment: McCullar signed a two-way contract with the Raptors on Thursday, Michael Scotto of HoopsHype.com reports.
injury.detail: McCullar quickly finds a new home after being waived by the Knicks in late October. The forward is expected to play a prominent role for Toronto's G League affiliate.

injury.shortComment: The Wizards announced Monday that Beekman sustained a right acromioclavicular joint injury and will be re-evaluated in approximately three weeks.
injury.detail: Beekman is set for an extended absence, with his re-evaluation timeline suggesting he could remain sidelined beyond the initial three-week window. The injury further limits Washington's backcourt depth, though Beekman's absence is unlikely to have a significant impact on standard fantasy leagues.

injury.shortComment: Champagnie (foot) is expected to miss several months, per Josh Robbins of The Athletic.
injury.detail: The forward underwent surgery Wednesday to address a fractured foot, and the Wizards hope Champagnie will be ready to return at some time around the All-Star break in February. The likes of Bilal Coulibaly, Tre Johnson and Bub Carrington will all be asked to help pick up the slack for the foreseeable future.

injury.shortComment: Okpara (illness) is available for Friday's game against Toronto.
injury.detail: Okpara will shed his questionable tag due to an illness and suit up Friday. However, the two-way player isn't guaranteed to see the floor.

injury.shortComment: Vukcevic (hip) has been ruled out for Monday's game against Memphis.
injury.detail: Vukcevic has yet to make his season debut due to a left hip injury. He can be considered week-to-week until the Wizards offer an update on his progress.

injury.shortComment: The Wizards announced Thursday that Watkins has undergone surgery for a torn ACL.
injury.detail: Watkins, a two-way player for the Wizards, suffered the injury during the Summer League. Although Washington has yet to offer a timetable for a return, a typical recovery time for the procedure is approximately 9-to-12 months. That leaves Watkins in serious jeopardy of missing most, if not all, of the 2026-27 season, and it remains to be seen if the team will continue keeping him around on a two-way roster spot while he's injured.

injury.shortComment: Mathurin (foot) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against Detroit.
injury.detail: Mathurin will miss a third straight contest due to plantar fasciitis in his left foot, which tends to be a lingering injury. Jordan Poole should remain in the backcourt rotation for the short-handed Pelicans moving forward.

injury.shortComment: McGowens (elbow) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against Detroit.
injury.detail: McGowens will miss a fourth consecutive contest due to an infection in his left elbow. It's unclear how far along he is in his recovery.

injury.shortComment: Murphy (knee) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against Detroit.
injury.detail: The star forward is missing a sixth consecutive contest with bilateral knee tendinopathy. Saddiq Bey should remain rostered in all fantasy leagues while Murphy is on the shelf.

injury.shortComment: Murray (ankle) is out for Friday's game against Memphis.
injury.detail: This was the expectation after the star guard requested a trade from the Pelicans earlier Friday. Given his standing with the club, Murray can be tentatively considered doubtful for future contests while New Orleans tries to find him another home.

injury.shortComment: Watford (ankle) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against Detroit.
injury.detail: Watford will miss a sixth consecutive contest due to a right ankle sprain. He remains without a definitive return timeline.

injury.shortComment: Duren (hamstring) has begun on-court activity and will be re-evaluated in two weeks, Hunter Patterson of The Athletic reports.
injury.detail: Duren is progressing in his rehab after suffering a right hamstring strain Oct. 23, though he'll remain on the inactive list for at least the next two weeks while ramping up toward a return to game action. Paul Reed should continue to play a sizable role in Duren's stead.

injury.shortComment: Holland is out for Tuesday's game against San Antonio due to a left knee contusion.
injury.detail: It's not clear as to when Holland picked up the injury, but it's significant enough to shut him down for at least one game. His next opportunity to return will arrive Wednesday in New Orleans.

injury.shortComment: Joe (hip) is out for Tuesday's game against the Spurs.
injury.detail: Joe has been sidelined since late October with a bruised hip. He has a short turnaround ahead of Wednesday's matchup in New Orleans for a possible return.

injury.shortComment: Prince (knee) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Spurs.
injury.detail: Prince made just his third appearance of the season during Saturday's 137-117 loss to Miami, finishing with two points (1-3 FG, 0-1 3Pt) and one assists in eight minutes. However, he'll now miss his 10th overall outing as he deals with soreness in his right knee. Prince's absence shouldn't have an impact on the rotation, and his next chance to suit up will come Wednesday versus New Orleans.

injury.shortComment: Robinson will be re-evaluated in one week due to a left quadriceps strain, Coty M. Davis of The Detroit News reports.
injury.detail: Robinson has gotten off to a strong start this season, though he's now expected to miss at least the next week after appearing in each of Detroit's first 12 regular-season games. The sharpshooter is averaging 17.4 points in 30.5 minutes per contest, and his absence will open up additional minutes for Kevin Huerter and Javonte Green.

injury.shortComment: Holmgren underwent a biological treatment Friday to address a small patellar tendon tear and will miss at least 8-10 weeks, Nick Crain of Slam reports.
injury.detail: This is another massive blow to an Oklahoma City squad that's already set to be without Jalen Williams (leg) and Cason Wallace (shoulder) for most, if not all, of the season. With Holmgren sidelined, Kenrich Williams, Jaylin Williams and Aday Mara are all candidates to see increased playing time. Two-way player Brooks Barnhizer could also see more minutes.

injury.shortComment: Sorber underwent an arthroscopic knee procedure Tuesday to address inflammation at the patellofemoral joint in his right knee, and he's expected to return to on-court activities in 6-8 weeks, Steve McGehee of News 9 Oklahoma City reports.
injury.detail: Once Sorber begins on-court work, there will be a ramp-up period before he's cleared for game-time action, so his absence will likely extend well beyond this initial 6-8-week window. Sorber was selected by the Thunder with the No. 15 pick in the 2025 NBA Draft, but he missed his entire rookie season after tearing the ACL in his right knee and has yet to play this season due to right knee issues.

injury.shortComment: Wallace underwent surgery Friday to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder and will be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season, Clemente Almanza of USA Today reports.
injury.detail: Wallace is expected to miss most, if not all, of the season. However, there's still a chance he will return late in the campaign after sustaining the shoulder injury in Sunday's win over the Clippers. With Jalen Williams (leg) also set to be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season, Alex Caruso (ankle) should see significant playing time once cleared to return. In the meantime, Jared McCain, Bennett Stirtz and Josh Dix are expected to see increased burn.

injury.shortComment: Williams (leg) underwent successful surgery Wednesday to "address a fractured left fibula and reconstruction of ankle ligaments following a fracture and dislocation." He will be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season, Tim MacMahon of ESPN.com reports.
injury.detail: Williams suffered the injury during Sunday's meeting with the Clippers and was taken off the court on a stretcher. It's unknown when the 25-year-old will be cleared to return, though the Thunder will presumably be overly cautious moving forward. Williams, who signed a five-year extension in July of 2025, has had a productive career, averaging 17.9 points, 4.6 rebounds, 4.4 assists and 1.3 steals over 30.9 minutes per contest. However, after playing at least 69 regular-season games in his first three years in the league, he has appeared in just 36 in the last two seasons combined. With the Thunder having one of the deepest rosters in the NBA, the team may look for more minutes from Jared McCain, Jaylin Williams, and Kenrich Williams for the remainder of the 2026-27 campaign.

injury.shortComment: Williams (back) is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against the Hawks, Clemente Almanza of USA Today reports.
injury.detail: Williams has missed the last seven games due to back spasms. He might return versus Atlanta, though it's unknown if he would rejoin the starting lineup. If Williams isn't back on the floor Wednesday, Aday Mara and Kenrich Williams would presumably continue to receive more playing time alongside Isaiah Hartenstein.

injury.shortComment: Flemings (back) is out for Wednesday's game against the Thunder.
injury.detail: Flemings is progressing well, having practiced Tuesday, but the Hawks are taking a cautious approach with the rookie first-round pick. With CJ McCollum on the shelf with a calf strain, Luguentz Dort is likely to enter the first unit while Aaron Wiggins takes on a larger role off the bench.

injury.shortComment: Gueye (foot) is ready to begin on-court activities and will be re-evaluated in four weeks, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
injury.detail: The team stated in July that the big man would remain sidelined for the next 3-to-4 months after undergoing surgery to repair a fractured left foot, and he's continuing to make progress in his rehab. A timetable for Gueye's 2026-27 debut has yet to be established, thought a date could come into focus following his next evaluation in mid-December.

injury.shortComment: Landale (hip) won't play Wednesday in Oklahoma City.
injury.detail: This will be Landale's second straight game on the sidelines, which should help Zuby Ejiofor remain in the rotation. For now, Landale should be considered questionable for Friday's meeting with the Hornets.

injury.shortComment: McCollum (calf) will miss at least four weeks, per Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network.
injury.detail: The veteran combo guard has been diagnosed with a left calf strain, and he's in line to miss the next month or so. Once rookie first-rounder Kingston Flemings (back) is healthy, he'll have a long runway as Atlanta's top point guard. Aaron Wiggins remains worth holding in nearly all fantasy leagues as well.

injury.shortComment: Newell underwent surgery Tuesday for a plantar plate tear in his left great toe, and he will be re-evaluated in approximately four months, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
injury.detail: Newell suffered the toe injury in the Nov. 4 win over Washington and is now set to miss an extended period. With Mouhamed Gueye (foot) expected to miss at least three more weeks, Aaron Wiggins and Corey Kispert could see a slight bump in minutes moving forward.

injury.shortComment: Veesaar was diagnosed with a torn right ACL and is expected to miss the 2026-27 season, the Hawks announced Monday.
injury.detail: Veesaar suffered the injury during a workout on Sept. 15, and an MRI confirmed the diagnosis. The No. 52 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, Veesaar was expected to spend a lot of time with Atlanta's G League affiliate this season.

injury.shortComment: Aldama (ankle) is probable for Wednesday's game against the Warriors.
injury.detail: Aldama practiced fully Tuesday and should be able to play through an ankle sprain Wednesday. He's set to return from a one-game absence, which could result in fewer minutes for Morez Johnson.

injury.shortComment: Biberovic (heel) is out for Wednesday's game against the Warriors.
injury.detail: Biberovic has yet to debut for the Mavs this season due to a right heel bursitis issue, and the fact that he continues to get ruled out a full day in advance of tipoff suggests he's still not close. Biberovic should be considered week-to-week moving forward.

injury.shortComment: Christie (ankle) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Warriors.
injury.detail: It's worth noting that Christie was a full practice participant Tuesday. His return from a two-game absence with an ankle sprain would likely lead to less playing time for Naji Marshall and Zaccharie Risacher on the wing.

injury.shortComment: Clayton (ankle) is listed as probable for Wednesday's game against the Warriors.
injury.detail: Clayton has only missed one game this season, and that's not expected to change Wednesday versus Golden State. The 23-year-old is coming off a strong showing, amassing 13 points, four rebounds, three assists and one steal in Sunday's 131-94 loss to Boston. Clayton also logged 23 minutes, though he might not play as much Wednesday with Kyrie Irving (knee) off the injury report.

injury.shortComment: De Larrea (knee) is listed as out for Wednesday's game against the Warriors.
injury.detail: De Larrea has only played four games during the 2026-27 campaign. There hasn't been any indication of when he will be cleared to return, so he should be considered week-to-week for now.

injury.shortComment: Lawal is doubtful for Wednesday's game against the Warriors due to tightness in his right groin.
injury.detail: Lawal is on track to sit out Wednesday's game. However, he's not a consistent part of the rotation, so his absence from the active roster won't impact fantasy leagues.

injury.shortComment: Lively (foot) is out for Wednesday's game against the Warriors.
injury.detail: Lively remains out indefinitely due to 2025 foot surgery. Meanwhile, Daniel Gafford is locked in as Dallas' top center.

injury.shortComment: Butler (knee) could return sometime between January and February as he continues recovering from a torn right ACL, Anthony Slater of ESPN reports.
injury.detail: Butler, who underwent surgery after suffering the injury Jan. 19, has progressed to individual court work but still has several rehabilitation milestones to clear. His next step involves landing comfortably after a game-speed jump. Coach Steve Kerr is hopeful Butler can rejoin Golden State for the latter portion of the season, though no official return date has been announced. The 37-year-old forward remains a significant part of the Warriors' plans and could provide a substantial boost during the second half of the campaign.

injury.shortComment: Curry has been diagnosed with an oblique abdominal tear and will be re-evaluated in two weeks, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
injury.detail: Curry suffered the injury early during Wednesday's loss to the Rockets, with head coach Steve Kerr saying after the game that the superstar point guard "tweaked" something in his abdominal area. Curry has never dealt with an injury of this nature, so the Warriors, who are off to a hot start spearheaded by Rookie of the Year candidate Yaxel Lendeborg, will likely proceed with caution. Brandin Podziemski, Brandon Williams (hamstring), De'Anthony Melton, Will Richard and Gary Payton (knee) are all candidates for increased roles until Curry is cleared to play again.

injury.shortComment: Green is questionable for Wednesday's game in Dallas due to inflammation in his right elbow.
injury.detail: Wednesday's game will be the first of a back-to-back set, so there's a chance Green could get hit with a maintenance day. If he is forced to the sidelines, Gui Santos would have a chance to start, and Georges Niang would have the chance for a bump in minutes.

injury.shortComment: Horford (back) is questionable for Wednesday's game against Dallas.
injury.detail: The 40-year-old big man could receive some load management for the first half of this back-to-back set. Charles Bassey could be a decent streaming option in fantasy leagues if Horford sits out.

injury.shortComment: Moody (knee) is progressing toward a potential return between December and January after rupturing his left patellar tendon in March, Anthony Slater of ESPN reports.
injury.detail: Moody has been limited to individual court work, but team sources indicate he's ahead of Jimmy Butler (knee) in the rehabilitation process and is expected to return before the veteran forward. The 24-year-old still has several recovery checkpoints to complete, and Golden State has not established an official timetable. His eventual return would help replenish a Warriors wing rotation that will open the season without both Moody and Butler.

injury.shortComment: Porzingis announced on his social media that he's stepping away from basketball.
injury.detail: Porzingis said he was looking forward to joining the Warriors, but his body didn't respond the way he wanted it too during his ramp-up process before the season. Additionally, he said he will work with the Warriors on a solution that "makes sense." Porzingis is making this decision to prioritize his health and will hopefully turn a corner soon on that front.

injury.shortComment: Williams (hamstring) has progressed to on-court activities and will be re-evaluated Saturday.
injury.detail: Williams sustained a left hamstring strain in the Nov. 9 win over New Orleans, and his next opportunity to play will come Sunday against Boston. LJ Cryer will likely continue seeing increased burn in Williams' stead.

injury.shortComment: Strawther (knee) was diagnosed with a left knee sprain Friday and will be re-evaluated in six weeks, Vinny Benedetto of The Denver Gazette reports.
injury.detail: Strawther suffered the injury in Wednesday's preseason game against the Clippers. The 24-year-old has appeared in 172 regular-season games for the Nuggets since entering the league in 2023, averaging 7.1 points, 2.0 rebounds and 1.1 assists over 16.2 minutes per contest. He was in line to compete for an expanded role during the 2026-27 campaign. While that may be the case once Strawther is cleared to suit up, Tyus Jones and potentially Ryan Nembhard are candidates to receive more minutes in the interim.

injury.shortComment: Head coach JJ Redick said he expects Walker (leg) to be available for Wednesday's game against the Jazz, Thuc Nhi Nguyen of the Los Angeles Times reports.
injury.detail: Walker won't play Tuesday against the Hornets due to some minor soreness in his right leg, but he'll return for the second leg of the back-to-back set Wednesday. Sandro Mamukelashvili, Jarred Vanderbilt and Kevon Looney will pick up the slack in his absence.

injury.shortComment: Reaves (heel) is out for Tuesday's game against the Hornets, Dave McMenamin of ESPN.com reports.
injury.detail: Reaves will miss a second consecutive matchup while tending to a bruised left heel. Quentin Grimes, Collin Sexton and Ziaire Williams should continue to see more minutes in Reaves' absence. His next opportunity to return will arrive Wednesday against Utah.

injury.shortComment: Hayes (knee) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Clippers.
injury.detail: Hayes will miss a second consecutive game due to a left knee strain, with his next chance to suit up coming Wednesday in the second half of the Jazz's back-to-back set. Mo Bamba is likely to remain in the starting lineup after faring well in his first start Sunday. On the year, Hayes is averaging 8.8 points, 6.0 rebounds, 1.6 assists and 1.3 blocks across 12 appearances (10 starts).

injury.shortComment: Jackson has been diagnosed with a torn MCL in his right knee and will be sidelined for 6-to-8 weeks, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
injury.detail: Jackson sustained the injury early in Monday's loss to Memphis, and he's now expected to miss at least a month and a half of action. The star big man's absence creates a major void in the Utah lineup, one that is likely to be filled by a timeshare of Jaxson Hayes (shoulder), Kyle Filipowski and Mo Bamba. The Jazz could also shift Lauri Markkanen (wrist), when healthy, to the center spot at times, perhaps allowing Ace Bailey to spend more time at power forward.

injury.shortComment: Markkanen has been diagnosed with a non-displaced fracture in his right hand and will be sidelined for at least one month, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
injury.detail: Markkanen has missed two straight games due to what was being described as a right wrist sprain, but it appears the issue was much worse than initially thought. The talented big man now joins Jusuf Nurkic (foot) and Jaren Jackson (knee) on Utah's long-term injury list, while Keyonte George's status moving forward is unclear while dealing with an ankle sprain. Given all of the injuries, Ace Bailey and Darryn Peterson will have to lead the offense, while Isaiah Collier, Brice Sensabaugh, Svi Mykhailiuk, Josh Okogie and Josh Green are candidates for increased roles.

injury.shortComment: Nurkic (toe) has begun participating in on-court activities as he continues recovering from a right foot injury sustained during an Oct. 4 preseason game against Denver. He will be re-evaluated in two weeks, the Jazz announced Friday.
injury.detail: Nurkic is progressing in his recovery, but the two-week re-evaluation timeline indicates he remains some distance from returning to game action. His absence should continue to create opportunities in Utah's frontcourt, with Jaxson Hayes and Mo Bamba among the players positioned to benefit from additional playing time. Nurkic's next evaluation will provide a clearer picture of his potential return date.

injury.shortComment: Achiuwa (ankle) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Suns, James Ham of ESPN 1320 Sacramento reports.
injury.detail: Achiuwa has missed the past two games for the Kings, but he was able to get through Tuesday's practice, so maybe he'll be able to return for Wednesday's game. If he is cleared to play, Dylan Cardwell's minutes might dip.

injury.shortComment: Hunter (hip) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Suns, James Ham of ESPN 1320 Sacramento reports.
injury.detail: Hunter missed Sunday's 125-103 loss to Oklahoma City due to left hip soreness, and that same issue has earned him a questionable tag versus Phoenix. If he's unable to suit up, Leaky Black, Emanuel Sharp, Keegan Murray and Malik Monk will continue to get more burn.

injury.shortComment: Raynaud (knee) will remain on the inactive list for Wednesday's game against the Suns.
injury.detail: Raynaud continues to get ruled out a full day in advance of tipoff, suggesting he's still not close. He should be considered week-to-week moving forward.

injury.shortComment: Simmons underwent successful surgery Tuesday to repair a torn right Achilles tendon, James Ham of ESPN 1320 Sacramento reports.
injury.detail: Simmons had a quality preseason, averaging 10.5 points, 4.0 rebounds and 4.0 assists over 17.4 minutes per contest (two games). The 30-year-old was on track to suit up for the Kings on opening night, though those plans were halted after he suffered a torn Achilles tendon during practice. Now, Simmons will focus on rehab. However, it's unknown what the future holds regarding his career in the NBA.

injury.shortComment: Williams underwent surgery Thursday to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder and will miss an extended period of time, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
injury.detail: This is a tough blow for the center with training camp right around the corner. With his status for Opening Night in jeopardy, this will put a lot of eyes on Oso Ighodaro and Khaman Maluach, with the latter already drawing buzz during the Summer League. More clarity on Williams' timeline should be known in the coming weeks.
